cta.quoteHtml: Offer it. It could be your Gest Dobra.
cta.text: If tomorrow you were to make one gesture that no one would notice, reward or keep score of, what would it be — and who would you offer it to?
cta.title: One Simple Gesture
ex.e1: You could ask a waiter to add another table's meal to your bill, choosing the guests at random. When they ask for their bill, the waiter could say: “This is a Gest Dobra — a gesture of kindness. Your meal has been paid for today. You owe nothing in return. If you ever feel like doing something kind for someone else, please pass it on.” If they would rather not accept the gift, they are entirely free to pay for themselves.
ex.e2: You can share your time, knowledge or skills. Help someone with a difficult task, prepare a snack for a colleague, invite them to lunch or support them through a hard day. Sometimes all it takes is to do something kind for someone, without expecting anything in return.
ex.e3: You could chat with an older person, help with a small technical problem, fill in a form for someone, clear snow from a stretch of pavement, mow a lawn, look after your neighbours' children so they can have some time to themselves, or do something else that makes everyday life a little better for those around you.
ex.e4: You can offer a small gesture to a complete stranger: buy someone a coffee, pay for their ticket or give them a little surprise. Simply to share some kindness.
ex.lead: Gest Dobra can take a material form, but its spirit is at its purest when no one except the recipient knows about it.
ex.title: Examples of Gest Dobra
footer: Gest Dobra — accept kindness and, if you wish, pass it on.

hero.claim2: It asks for no favour in return
hero.lead: Gest Dobra — Polish for “a gesture of kindness” — is a freely given act of kindness from one person to another.
hero.title: Accept kindness.
how.lead: You don't need a great deal of money or resources. One tangible act of kindness is enough, offered without expecting gratitude, recognition or payment.
how.s1: Someone has done something kind for you, with no strings attached — not because you earned it or will return the favour. Accept the gift. Perhaps one day, through you, kindness will reach someone else.
how.s1alt: Two hands passing a red heart in soft light
how.s2: Look around. Who near you needs help, time, attention or support — a simple human gesture? Perhaps there is someone you would like to be kind to for no particular reason. Or someone you know will pass that kindness on.
how.s2alt: A person sitting on a bench, paying close attention to the people around them
how.s3: Do something kind within your means, simply to give another person the chance to experience kindness. If you hand them a Gest Dobra card, it becomes a symbol of that gesture and an invitation to pass kindness on to others. That is how Gest Dobra keeps going.
how.s3alt: A person passing on a Gest Dobra card, symbolising kindness continuing its journey
how.title: How Can You Pass Gest Dobra On?
idea.c1: When someone gives us something without expecting payment, we often feel an immediate urge to return the favour. Gest Dobra interrupts that calculation. It lets us accept kindness without feeling that we have to “settle the score” straight away.
idea.c2: Gest Dobra is not reserved for those who need help, are more vulnerable or are going through a difficult time. It is for people. For everyone. It does not label, judge or divide us into categories.
idea.c3: Gest Dobra is not a marketing campaign, a discount or a promotional freebie. It might take the form of an item or service freely given, a bill paid, practical help, time, attention, standing up for someone more vulnerable or quietly solving someone's problem.
idea.c4: Kindness should not create new problems. Gest Dobra is an expression of goodwill and must not become a burden on you or your loved ones. What matters is not the size of the gesture, but the intention and the willingness to share thoughtfully, within your means.
idea.c5: A Gest Dobra cannot be demanded, obtained by manipulation or expected as an entitlement. Its essence is that it is freely given: an expression of the giver's choice and an invitation to the person receiving it.

idea.title: What Does Gest Dobra Really Mean?
